items.e: TO THE AMORITES. The lamed prefixed to the word emori (Amorite) is vocalized with a kamatz . Its reference is to the famous Amorites Sihon and Og. There were no kings among the Canaanites as great as they. Whose height was like the height of the cedars (Amos 2:9) is proof of this.
AND MOAB WAS SORE AFRAID. Va-yagar means was afraid. Guru lakhem (be ye afraid) (Job 19:29) is similar.

AND MOAB WAS OVERCOME WITH DREAD. Va-yakatz (overcome with dread) has the same meaning as a similarly spelled word whose letters are inverted. U-nekitzennah (and vex it) in Let us go up against Judah, and vex it (Is. 7:6) is similar.
UNTO THE ELDERS OF MIDIAN. It is possible that the five Midianite kings are these same elders.
NOW WILL THIS MULTITUDE LICK UP…AS THE OX LICKETH UP. Yelachakhu (will…lick up) and ki-lechokh (as…licketh up) are two different conjugations.
TO PETHOR. Pethorah means to Pethor. Compare, mitzrayemah (to Egypt) (Gen. 37:25).

TO THE LAND OF THE CHILDREN OF HIS PEOPLE. Who were Arameans. Scripture similarly states, from Pethor of Aram-naharaim (Deut. 23:5). The midrash identifies Balaam with Bela. [However, the identification is untenable] because Balaam was an Aramean. If we identify Balaam with Bela because of Beor his father, then, lo and behold, the son of Ahasuerus lived before Ahasuerus. They are definitely two different people.
WHICH IS BY THE RIVER. The reference is to Aram-naharaim.
THE FACE OF THE EARTH. I have already explained the meaning of this expression.

CURSE ME. The word arah (curse) is an imperative. It comes from a double root with one of the double letters missing. The same is true of with the word kavah (curse) in curse me (v. 18). The word kov (curse) is vocalized according to the paradigm of shemor (keep). Kavah in kavah li (curse me) minus the heh follows the paradigm of shechav (lie), rekhav (ride), and tzelach (rested on).

THAT WE MAY SMITE THEM. Nakkeh (that we may smite them) is an infinitive. The fact that it ends in a heh is no argument against the latter, for the word le-khalle (to finish), in to finish the transgression (Dan. 9:24) is similar.

IS CURSED. The silent vav of yu’ar (is cursed) is in place of a dagesh , which is in place of the missing double letter. Compare, yusav (turned about) in turned about upon the cummin (Is. 28:27). There is no other word like it in this form, because of the rules concerning gutturals.
THE ELDERS OF MOAB. The wise men.

WITH THE REWARDS OF DIVINATION IN THEIR HAND. Rabbi Samuel Ha-Nagid the Sephardi, of blessed memory, said that the meaning of u-kesamim (with the reward of divination) is payment for divination. He offers as proof the word be-yadam (in their hand). However, he says nothing. U-kesamim be-yadam is to be taken literally. Scripture tells us that Balak sent diviners like himself to the diviner [Balaam]. Furthermore, Balaam would not be able to tarry, saying, “I can not find a propitious day, and a propitious hour to go and curse,” for the messengers were members of his guild. In his right hand is the instrument of divination (ha-kesom) (Ez. 21:27) is proof that u-kesamim be-yadam is to be taken literally.
AND I WILL BRING YOU BACK WORD. After you spend the night here.

AND GOD CAME. Out of regard for Israel, for God knew the coming incident of ba’al pe’or . Now if Balaam had cursed them then, all of the world would have said that the plague came because of Balaam’s curse.

WHAT MEN ARE THESE. This was a way of opening and starting a conversation. It is similar to Where is Abel thy brother (Gen. 4:9). Now Cain denied [knowledge of Abel’s whereabouts]. However, God told him, the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth out unto Me (Gen. 4 :10).
FOR THEY ARE BLESSED. Its meaning is, you cannot curse them, for I have blessed them.

THE PRINCES OF BALAK. Scripture does not mention the elders of Midian, for Balak was the protagonist and he sent the messengers to Balaam. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen the Spaniard, of blessed memory, says that even though the yod is the sign of the object it can only come with a nun . Compare, ha-lehorgeni (thinkest thou to kill me) (Ex. 2:14). It does not read ha-lehorgi . However, he forgot le-titti (to give me) in to give me leave to go with you [our verse] and yabbemi (perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto me) in he will not perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto me (Deut. 25:7). Rabbi Jonah the grammarian says that the yod of le-titti is superfluous, but what he says is incorrect.
[TO COME WITH US.] Its meaning is, to go with us from his place.

MORE. The word rabbim (more) is to be taken literally, or it is to be rendered as great. Compare, to all the officers (rav) of his house (Esth. 1:8) and The city of the great king (rav) (Ps. 48:3), that is, David, for the city was called the city where David encamped (Is. 29:1).
FOR I WILL PROMOTE THEE. With money.

AND WHATSOEVER THOU SAYEST UNTO ME I WILL DO. If this is necessary for you to curse them. Balaam’s statement, If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold , is proof that the meaning of For I will promote is, and I will promote you with money.

HIS HOUSE FULL. Melo beto means his house full. Melo khol ha-aretz kevodo (the whole earth is full of His glory) (Is. 6:3) is similar. Many err who thought that the meaning of the latter is that the contents of the earth is God’s glory, as in the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof (Ps. 24:1).

SMALL OR GREAT. The words ketannah (small) and gedolah (great) are adjectives. However, the nouns are missing. But the rich man answers impudent (Prov. 18:23) and, and his food fat (Hab. 1:16) are similar.

HERE. In this place. The Gaon, of blessed memory, says: Should someone argue and say, “How could God tell Balaam rise up, go with them (v. 20) after telling him Thou shalt not go with them (12)?” Then we can answer him that God did not want Balaam to go with these messengers but to wait until Balak sent messengers more honorable than they. However, I believe that there is no need for the Gaon’s interpretation. Its meaning is similar to God telling Israel, Send thou men (Num. 13:2) and go up, take possession (Deut. 1:21). Israel did not believe. On the contrary, they said, Let us send men before us (Deut. 1:22). Moses then asked God. God told him, Send thou men (Num. 13:2). Now after God told Balaam, thou shalt not curse the people (v. 12), what need did Balaam have to say, that I may know what the Lord will speak unto me more (v. 19)? Balaam had an evil thought in his heart. God told him go with the men, but take care that you do not say anything save that which I will tell you. And God’s anger was kindled because he went (v. 22) is proof that my explanation is correct.
AND SADDLED. By command.
FOR AN ADVERSARY AGAINST HIM. I have already explained in the Book of Job that the adversary was an angel. The words of the Gaon that the adversary was a human being do not help or hinder.
OUT OF THE WAY. Which was trodden. The ass went into a field wherein there was no path.
TO TURN HER INTO THE WAY. The phrase le-hatotah ha-derekh (to turn her the way) is abridged. It means to turn her into the way.

IN A HOLLOW WAY BETWEEN THE VINEYARDS. The word mishol (hollow way) is to be interpreted according to its context, for it is not found again in Scripture. It should be explained as the Aramaic translation renders it.
AND SHE THRUST HERSELF UNTO THE WALL. Va-tillachetz is to be rendered, and she thrust herself.
UNTO THE WALL. The reference is to the fence.
AND HE SMOTE HER AGAIN. For he had already hit her when she turned into the field.

AND THE LORD OPENED THE MOUTH OF THE ASS. The rabbis, of blessed memory, said that ten things were created on Sabbath eve at twilight. I believe that this means that God specifically decreed the creation of these miraculous phenomena, for they are beyond the laws of nature. The Gaon says that the ass did not speak. Rabbi Samuel the son of Hofni attacked the Gaon. However, Rabbi Samuel the Spanish poet tried to save the one who was attacked. Note, the rationalists had a need for a non-literal interpretation of our text, for they said that God would not create signs in the world to change the laws which he created. He would do so only to justify his prophet. However, they did not speak the truth, for, look, a miracle was done for Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, who were not prophets. Some of them say that Balaam was a prophet. However, the truth is that his prophecy was because of Israel’s glory, for Balaam was a diviner. Indeed, this is how Scripture refers to him. Some say that Balaam knew the mind of the heavenly beings and was able to channel them by images that he made. This is the meaning of and he whom thou cursest is cursed (v. 6). However, it appears to me that Balaam was an astrologer. When Balaam saw in the star of a given person that an evil time had befallen him, he would curse him. When evil befell the one whom he cursed, then those who witnessed and heard the imprecation thought that the evil came because of Balaam’s curse. The fact that Balaam spoke with guile to the lords of Balak is proof of this. The meaning of I can not go beyond the word of the Lord my God (v. 18) is, it is not in the hand of any created being to change a deed or a decree of God. The secret is, the part can not change a part. It is only the decree of the All which can change the decree of the part. I cannot reveal this secret for it is very deep. The correct interpretation is, the ass spoke. If you understand the secret of the angels of Abraham and of Jacob, then you will understand the truth.
[WITH HIS STAFF.] Scripture states this because Balaam first hit her with a small piece of wood or with a strap.
TIMES. I have already explained the meaning of the term regalim (times).
HAST MOCKED. I have already explained the term hitalalt (hast mocked).
ALL THY LIFE LONG. This means from the day that you started to ride.
WAS I EVER WONT. The meaning of ha-hasken hiskanti is, was I ever wont. Its import is, was this my manner. The word hasken (acquaint) in Acquaint (hasken) now thyself with him (Job 22:21) is similar.
THEN THE LORD OPENED. As in the case of Elisha’s young man (II Kings 6:17). God added to the light of his eyes or first struck him blind.
AND BOWED HIS HEAD. I have already explained its meaning.

BECAUSE THY WAY IS CONTRARY UNTO ME. The meaning of yarat (contrary) is perverse. The word yirteni (twists me) in And twists me by the hands of the wicked (Job 16:11), which comes from the root resh, tet, heh , is similar. If yirteni comes from the root yod, resh, tet , then it should be vocalized like ye’atani (He hath covered me) (Is. 61:10). Yarat and yirteni have similar meanings even though they come from two different roots. We find the same to be the case with the word ye’atani ( Ibid .), which is vocalized like the word ye’atzani (given me counsel) (Ps. 16:7). Ye’atani is similar in meaning to oteh (coverest) in (Who coverest Thyself with light) (Ps. 104:2).
AND THE ASS SAW ME. Va-tirani is spelled with a pattach in place of a tzere . It should have been vocalized va-tireni . There are many such cases.
UNLESS. The word ulai (unless) has many meanings. Here it means unless. The word even is evidence that the ass died after she spoke.

AND SAVED HER ALIVE. Scripture is being brief. Its meaning is, as I killed her I would have killed you, or I would have killed you and left her alive. The above is explained by the following. When a person sees an angel, he dies. And my life is preserved (Gen. 32:1), and the words of Manoah are proof. How much more so the case of a beast that has nothing in common with the spirit of an angel as a human being does.
GO WITH THE MEN. With these men.
BUT ONLY. The word efes means only. The word efes (howbeit) in Howbeit there shall be no needy among you (Deut. 15: 4) and in Howbeit (efes) the people…are fierce (Num. 13:28) is similar.

WHEREFORE CAMEST THOU NOT UNTO ME. The word halakhta is to be rendered camest because it is followed by elai (unto me). The same applies, as I have already explained, to the word va-ysar (departed) (I Sam. 15:6).
KIRIATH-HUZOTH. It is the name of a province.
BAMOTH-BAAL. This is to be identified with Bamotharnon (the high places of Arnon) (Num. 21:28).
AND HE SAW FROM THENCE THE UTMOST PART OF THE PEOPLE. For they camped on all four compass points.

SEVEN ALTARS. There are deep secrets which only a few can fathom. The number seven occurs with regard to days, months, years; the seven lambs offered for a burnt offering; the seven sprinklings. God also told Job, take unto you seven bullocks and seven rams (Job 42:8). When the complete is added to the complete, then a spirit of understanding is newly created. The intelligent will understand what I speak of.
ON EVERY ALTAR A BULLOCK AND A RAM. On each and every altar. Scripture is being brief. It is short for, on one of the many altars.
WILL COME. Yikkareh (will come) is derived from li-kerati (to meet me).
AND WHATSOEVER HE SHOWETH ME. The word devar is connected to mah .

AND HE WENT TO A BARE HEIGHT. The manner in which the Aramaic translator renders shefi (bare) is known. He translates shefi as alone. Now shefi is alone; it is also without a brother. Other say that the word shefi means broken in heart (Ps. 109:16). They say that the word shefi is related to shuppu (corrode) in and his bones corrode (Job 33:21). However, I believe that the word shefi is related to shefayim (high hills) in upon the high hills is heard (Jer. 3:20). The word is found spelled both with a yod and with an alef . We find the same thing with the word peta’im (simple) (Prov. 1:4). The meaning of va-elekh shefi (and he went to a bare height) is, he went to a high hill. The word el (to) has been omitted from the phrase. We find the same in va-yavo yerushalayim (and he came to Jerusalem) (I Kings 3:15) and in nase’u ha-am hazerot (the people journeyed unto Hazeroth) (Num. 11:35). There are many such instances. Observe, Balaam was divining when he went, for Scripture clearly states, he went not, as at other times to meet with enchantments (Num. 24:1). See, I have given you a hint regarding a sealed secret.
AND I HAVE OFFERED UP A BULLOCK AND A RAM ON EVERY ALTAR. By command.
AND HE TOOK UP HIS PARABLE, AND SAID. The parable referred to is, For from the top of rocks I see him (v. 9).
FROM THE MOUNTAINS OF THE EAST. The word kedem means east.
COME, CURSE ME JACOB. “And he said” has been omitted from our clause. We find many such instances in the Song of Songs. This is an abridged style.

EXECRATE ISRAEL. Scripture repeats itself as is its custom. Its manner is to employ different words to express the same thought. It repeats itself for emphasis. The word zo’amah (execrate) should have been vocalized like the word zokhrah (remember) in Remember unto me, O my God (Neh. 5:19). However, since the ayin was vocalized with a pattach because it is a guttural, a cholam rather than a short kamatz was placed between it and the zayin .

HOW SHALL I CURSE, WHOM GOD HATH NOT CURSED. The word kabboh means to curse. Its heh is in place of a vav . It is like the heh in oholoh (his tent) (Gen. 12:8) and the heh in fera’oh (let them loose) in for Aaron had let them loose (Ex. 32:25). Kabboh comes from a double root. Its full form is kavevo (they curse him). Compare, savevo (they surrounded him) although it is irregular.
AND HOW SHALL I EXECRATE, WHOM GOD HATH NOT EXECRATED. The words ezam (shall I execrate) and za’am (execrate) come from the root, zayin, ayin, mem (anger). Scripture repeats itself.

FOR FROM THE TOP OF THE ROCKS I SEE HIM. Balaam said this because he was high up on the hill. He went not, as at other times, to meet with enchantments. But he set his face toward the wilderness (Num. 24:1) and not toward the high place is proof that my interpretation of shefi is correct. It is also likely that from the top of the rocks is a parable symbolizing the decrees that come down from heaven. For Balaam in his wisdom saw that this nation would stand alone and not intermingle with other nations that would overpower her and try to force her to give up God’s Torah, as the nations did.
AND SHALL NOT BE RECKONED AMONG THE NATIONS. I will explain this in my comments on When the Most High gave to the nations their inheritance (Deut. 32:8).
WHO HATH COUNTED. It is a wonder that Israel is not counted with the nations, when they are a nation as numerous as the sand. It is likely for a small nation not to be counted.
THE DUST OF JACOB. Its meaning is: Jacob is as numerous as the dust of the earth.
OR NUMBERED THE STOCK OF ISRAEL? One standard. It means the same as thou shalt see but the utmost part of them, and shalt not see them all (v. 13).

[LET ME DIE THE DEATH OF THE RIGHTEOUS, AND LET MINE END BE LIKE HIS!] The Aramaic translator beautifully explained the meaning of yesharim (the righteous).I believe that Balaam wanted to die. He wanted his end to be like the end of Israel, who are God’s portion and are not ruled by the stars, for he was a magician. Others say that mine end repeats let me die . Balaam wanted to die like the righteous of Israel, for he knew that he would die by the sword. The Gaon says that Who hath counted refers to God. Our verse means: You who are able to count the dust of Jacob, give me the death of the righteous. However, if this is so, then what meaning is there to Or numbered the stock of Israel ? Many explain that rova (the stock of) is similar in meaning to rivi , which means my lying down. Compare, Thou measurest my going about and my lying down (rivi) (Ps. 139:3). They explain that the dust of Jacob refers to the time that Jacob journeys.

[THOU HAST BLESSED THEM ALTOGETHER.] It is normal usage to place the infinitive first in the perfect and then the imperfect. The reverse is true in the imperative. However, there are irregular phrases such as u-verakhta barekh (thou hast blessed them altogether) (Num. 24:10); and yava vo (and he shall come on) in and he shall come on, and overflow, as he passeth through (Dan. 11:1).
BUT THE UTMOST. The meaning of efes katzehu is, but the utmost.

AND CURSE ME THEM. Ve-kovno (and curse them) is irregular. According to the rules of grammar the imperative is the same as the imperfect. The only difference between them is the prefix. Compare, yirdefehu (he shall pursue him); yirdefenu (he shall pursue him); yirdefuhu (they shall pursue him); and yirdefo (shall pursue him) in The enemy shall pursue him (Hos. 8:3). However, kovno comes with a nun vocalized with a cholam joined to the root. According to Rabbi Judah, the first grammarian, the word kovno comes from the root kof, bet, nun . If this is the case, then kovno cannot be an imperative, for we do not find such a vocalization in the kal . Perhaps kovno is an infinitive vocalized like the word shomro (keep) in and because He would keep the oath (Deut. 7:8).
AND HE TOOK UP HIS PARABLE. The reference is to like the lofty horns of the wild-ox (v. 22) and a people that riseth up as a lioness (v. 24).

GIVE EAR UNTO ME. The word adai (unto me) is related to the word ad (unto). The word adai (unto Me) in Yet have ye not returned unto Me (Amos 4:6) is similar. Scripture repeats itself. The vav in beno tzippor (son of Zippor) is superfluous. It is similar to the vav of le-mayeno (a fountain) in into a fountain of waters (Ps. 114:8).
[GOD IS NOT A MAN.] Balaam said this in response to Balak’s request, and curse me them from thence (v. 13). However, Balaam had already told him, God hath not cursed (v. 8).
WHEN HE HATH SAID, WILL HE NOT DO IT? His word.
OR WHEN HE HATH SPOKEN. A word.
BEHOLD, I AM BIDDEN TO BLESS. Barekh (to bless) is an infinitive. It has the same meaning as a noun.
AND WHEN HE HATH BLESSED. U-verekh (and when he hath blessed) is a verb in the perfect. Its meaning is, when God pronounced a blessing, I cannot call it back.

NONE HATH BEHELD INIQUITY IN JACOB. I believe that Balak learned from this utterance to send Moabite women into the camp of Israel. Scripture’s meaning is that God is not like a man that he should repent (v. 19), for He did not see iniquity in Israel. However, if there be iniquity in Israel, then God’s word will not come to pass, for all of God’s words are conditional unless accompanied by an oath. Compare, At one instant I may speak concerning a nation…to build and to plant…but if it do evil in My sight…then I repent of the good, wherewith I said I would benefit it . (Jer. 18:7-10). This is the meaning of Balaam’s statement.

NEITHER HATH ONE SEEN PERVERSENESS IN ISRAEL. Scripture repeats itself. The word amal (perverseness) is brother to aven (iniquity). Amal (perverseness) is so called because iniquity ( aven ) ultimately leads to it. Look, as long as God does not see iniquity in Jacob, He is with Israel.
AND THE SHOUTING FOR THE KING IS AMONG THEM. In the camp of Israel. The reference is to and when ye blow an alarm (tru’ah) (Num. 10:5).
GOD WHO BROUGHT THEM FORTH OUT OF EGYPT. This God who brought them out of Egypt is mighty and showed his miracles in Egypt.

LIKE THE LOFTY HORNS OF THE WILD-OX. Ke-to’afot re’em (like the lofty horns of the wild-ox) is similar to karne re’em (the horns of the wild-ox) (Deut. 33:17). The meaning of to’afot is , the might of. To’afot (the heights of) in The heights of the mountain are His also (Ps. 95:4) is similar. It is also possible that the meaning of ve-to’afot harim lo (the heights of the mountains are His) is, the horns of the mountains are also His. The meaning of ve-kehsef to’afot lakh (and precious silver unto thee) (Job 22:25) is, and silver, as mighty as the mountains. Scripture reads lo (to him). [It means to them.] Compare, and the shouting for the King is among them (v. 21). It means that this God made Israel strong. God did all this for them because Israel cleaves to God and does not seek anything from anyone but the Lord, for they have no need for an enchanter and a diviner.
NOW IT IS SAID OF JACOB. Ka-et (now) is to be rendered, like this time. Its meaning is: at all times it will be told to them without the assistance of an enchanter.

WHAT HATH GOD WROUGHT. Mah pa’al el (what hath God wrought) is to be rendered, what God shall do. All things decreed, even those decreed for the future, are decreed in the past. Hence Scripture employs a perfect ( pa’al) . This will be told to Israel prophetically. What is told in prophecy is the truth.
OF JACOB AND OF ISRAEL. Scripture repeats itself in a prophetic utterance. Compare, From the top of Senir and Hermon (Song of Songs 4:8).

BEHOLD A PEOPLE THAT RISETH UP AS A LIONESS. This hints that Israel will conquer the kings of Canaan. It seems most logical to interpret it this way regarding a soon-to-occur event, such as the war against Midian. A war like it was unprecedented. No Israelites were lost in this war and five kings died in it, along with thirty-two thousand females who never slept with a man.

AND DRINK THE BLOOD OF THE SLAIN. The spoil and all their wealth. According to the midrashic interpretation it means that Moses would not die until he ate of the prey. Scripture similarly reads: Afterward shalt thou be gathered unto thy people (Num. 31:2).
THAT THOU MAYEST CURSE ME THEM. Ve-kabbota (that thou mayest curse) comes from a double root. Compare, ve-sabboti ani (therefore I turned) (Eccles. 2:20).
UNTO THE TOP OF PEOR. Balaam did not seek to use sorcery, so God’s spirit came upon him. Balaam acted like this because he saw that there is no enchantment with Jacob (Num. 23:23).
BUT HE SET HIS FACE TOWARD THE WILDERNESS. Where Israel was, in the plains of Moab.

DWELLING TRIBE BY TRIBE. He saw all the standards. Some say that Balaam had a diabolical eye. Such people are called evildoers. Balaam did evil by employing his diabolic eye. I have already made my opinion known to you.
AND HE TOOK UP HIS PARABLE. This means he lifted up his voice and uttered his parable. The parable was, As valleys stretched out (v. 6).

THE SAYING OF. The word ne’um means the saying of. Compare, va-yimamu ne’um (and say: He saith) (Jer. 23:31). Some say that who heareth and also Who seeth means who hears and who sees by divination. However, it most likely refers to that which is heard and seen in a prophetic dream. Compare Eliphaz’s statement, A form was before mine eyes; I heard a still voice (Job 4:16).

WHOSE EYE IS OPENED. The word shetum (opened) has no brother. It can be interpreted only in context. Shetum is the opposite of setum (shut). Some say that Balaam had only one eye. However, this is a midrashic interpretation.
FALLEN DOWN. Compare, a deep sleep fell upon Abram (Gen. 15:12).
YET WITH OPENED EYES. Even though he sleeps, he sees with his eyes. Compare, [ I sleep ] but my heart waketh (Cant. 5:2).
HOW GOODLY. Tovu (goodly) is a verb in the perfect. It is similar to oru (are brightened) in how mine eyes have brightened (I Sam. 14:29).

STRETCHED OUT. The tet of nittayu (stretched out) rceives a dagesh to compensate for the nun of natah (stretched), which is swallowed. Scripture reads stretched out because there are rivers that turn here and there and have trees over them.
AS ALOES. Ahalim (aloes) is similar to the word ahalot (aloes) in myrrh, and aloes (Ps. 45:9). Note, Balaam compares the tents to stretched-out rivers.
AS CEDARS. Scripture repeats itself. Balaam mentions cedars in the sense of He shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon (Ps. 92:13).
WATER SHALL FLOW. Look, mayim is in the singular. Compare, the water of (mai) sprinkling was not dashed (zorak) against him (Num. 19:13).
FROM HIS BRANCHES. Dalyo (his branches) is similar to daliyyotav (his branches) (Jer. 11:16).
AND HIS SEED SHALL BE IN MANY WATERS. Like seed saturated with water. This means he shall flourish and grow every day.
AND HIS KING SHALL BE HIGHER THAN AGAG. This is a prophecy regarding Saul, Israel’s first king, for prior to Saul there were judges but no kings.

GOD WHO BROUGHT HIM FORTH. The meaning of our verse is: the God who brought him [Israel] out of Egypt made him as powerful as the lofty horns of the wild-ox. Let not the one who would dispute this claim that the word him refers to God, because Scripture earlier used the plural form motzi’am (brought them forth) when it stated, God who brought them forth (Num. 23:22). For such is the style of Scripture. Compare, And they sit at Thy feet; he receives (yissa) Thy words (Deut. 33:3); and How long will this (ha-zeh) people despise Me (yena’atzuni) (Num. 14:11). There are many such instances.
HE SHALL EAT UP THE NATIONS THAT ARE HIS ADVERSARIES. The reference is to the kings of Canaan.

AND SHALL BREAK THEIR BONES IN PIECES. Garem means a bone. Yigarem means he shall break their bones. The word itzemo (hath broken his bones) (Jer. 50:17) is similar. So too is the word mesa’ef (shall lop) in Shall lop the boughs with terror (Is. 10:33) and tefa’er (go over the boughs) in thou shalt not go over the boughs (Deut. 24 :20).

AND PIERCE THEM THROUGH WITH HIS ARROWS. Each one of his arrows shall pierce. So too, But the righteous are secure as a young lion (Prov. 28:1); Its branches run over the wall (Gen. 49:22); Blessed be every one that blesseth thee (v. 9). The latter means, everyone that blesses you wil be blessed. So too, and cursed be everyone that curseth thee ( Ibid .).
HE COUCHED. The meaning of our verse is: Israel will inherit Canaan, after which the land will be quiet.
SHALL ROUSE HIM UP. I have already explained this.
AND HE SMOTE HIS HANDS TOGETHER. Va-yispok (and he smote) is similar to safeku (clap) in All that pass by clap Their hands at thee (Lam. 2:15).

AND I WILL ANNOUNCE TO THEE. Some say that its meaning is: I will advise you with regard to the daughters of Moab. However, this is far-fetched, for Scripture says, in the end of days . I believe that we should take it according to its plain meaning; namely, I will advise you, so that you know what you should do, for this people will do this to your people.
AND KNOWETH THE KNOWLEDGE OF THE MOST HIGH. By prophecy, not through enchantment.
I SEE HIM, BUT NOT NOW. It appears to me that this prophecy refers to King David. Balaam said but not now, for it referred to an event four hundred years later.
I BEHOLD HIM, BUT NOT NIGH. Scripture repeats itself. The star and the sceptre are the parable.
THERE SHALL STEP FORTH A STAR. There are images of stars that step forth in the sky that never existed and were never known.

AND A SCEPTRE SHALL ARISE. The reference is to a royal sceptre.I believe that shall step means that the star shall be seen making its way, as in The stars in their courses (Jud. 5:20). Many explained that the reference is to the messiah. The ancients said that Sanherib mixed up the nations. However, note that Scripture speaks of Moab, Amalek, and Asshur. Furthermore, why does Balaam conclude with and shall afflict Eber (v. 24)? On the contrary, Balaam should have ended his parable with There shall step forth a star out of Jacob . Those who lack intelligence think that anyone who explains that There shall step forth a star refers to King David denies the coming of the messiah. Far be it, far be it, for the messiah is clearly stated in the prophecy of Daniel. I have already explained that Daniel first mentions the coming into existence of the Greek kings and the arising of the Hasmoneans. He mentions the existence of the second temple, the years of the siege, the exile, and the salvation. He notes these things in order. There is no conceivable need for another prophet, since we have the words of Moses, who is the most important prophet: If any of thine that are dispersed be in the uttermost parts of heaven… the Lord thy God will bring thee (Deut. 30:4,5).
AND SHALL SMITE THROUGH THE CORNERS OF MOAB. This is what David did.
AND BREAK DOWN. The word karkar (break down) is similar to mekarkar kir (Is. 22:5), the meaning of which is, breaking the wall. It is similar to the word mesa’ef (shall lop) (Is. 10:33).

THE SONS OF SETH. People. Seth was the most important son of Adam, for Noah was descended from him. Yitzchaki says that the reference is to the Amonites and the Moabites, and that Scripture repeats itself. He also says that the word Seth is derived from the word shet (buttocks) in and with buttocks uncovered (Is. 20:4) and that it alludes to the daughters of Lot. However, this appears to me to be farfetched, for shet refers to the backside, which is the foundation of the body. Compare, ki ha-shatot yeharesun (When the foundations are destroyed) (Ps. 11:3). Many others have explained that the word shet (Seth) in all the sons of Seth , is related to the word ha-shatot (foundations) in When the foundations are destroyed . It means that the cities will be destroyed. This interpretation is not far-fetched.

AND EDOM SHALL BE A POSSESSION. The word yereshah (possession) is related to the word torishu (drive out) in But if ye will not drive out (Num. 33:55). Yereshah is a noun vocalized according to the pattern of the word levenah (tile) in take thee a tile (Ezek. 4:1). It is in place of an adjective. Compare the word shemamah (desolation) in and it shall be a desolation (Is. 17:9). We know that David’s hand overpowered Edom and Mount Seir.
AND OUT OF JACOB SHALL ONE HAVE DOMINION. A ruler shall arise out of Jacob.
AND SHALL DESTROY THE REMNANT FROM THE CITY. From every city. Its meaning is, from Edom. The reference is to Joab, for Scripture clearly states, and had smitten every male in Edom (I Kings 11:15).

AND HE LOOKED ON AMALEK. Via prophecy. The first of the nations is the parable. It means Amalek was the first nation to wage war against Israel, but his end shall be utter destruction. This took place in the days of Saul, who slew man and woman, infant and suckling (I Sam. 15:3) and old men. Many explain that the meaning of the first of the nations is that Amalek was considered to be the head of the nations. However, this was not the case.

AND HE LOOKED ON THE KENITE. The family of Jethro. Scripture writes, These are the Kenites (I Chron. 2:55) and Now Heber the Kenite (Jud. 4:11). And though thy nest be set in the rock is the parable. The latter repeats the preceding clause. Its meaning is, though your dwelling place be as high as the nest of a bird, it will not save you.

KAIN SHALL BE WASTED. Le-va’er (wasted) is similar to the word le-va’er (eaten up) in it shall again be eaten up (Is. 6:13); and yeva’er (sweepeth) in as a man sweepeth away dung (I Kings 14:10); and u-vi’arta (so shalt thou put away) in So shalt thou put away the evil from thee (Deut. 13:6). Kain and the Kenite are one and the same.

[HOW LONG? ASSHUR SHALL CARRY THEE AWAY CAPTIVE.] Balaam, as it were, said: How long shall Asshur carry thee away captive? He will not let go of you until you are wasted. Asshur is feminine. Asshur is short for the camp of Asshur. Compare, va-tipple sheva va-tikkachem (and the Sabeans made a raid) (Job 1:15); Va-ta’arokh yisra’el (and Israel…put the battle in array) (I Sam. 17:21).

AND HE TOOK UP HIS PARABLE, AND SAID. The reference is to But ships shall come from the coast of Kittim (v. 24). When Balaam mentioned that the Kenite would be carried away captive, he also said that a time would come when Asshur would be afflicted and Eber along with him. The latter refers to the Hebrews that Asshur carried away captive, for the Kenites lived with the Israelites. The interpretation of the Aramaic translation is well known. However, it is not the practice of Scripture to mention the word ever without the word nahar (river) following it. Some explain that tzim (ships) is a plural. It is related to the word tzi (ship) in gallant ship (Is. 33:21). Others say that the word tzim is related to the word tziyim (wild-cats) in And the wild-cats shall meet with the jackals (Is. 34:14). Balaam compared the Kittim to wild-cats because people will be gripped by fear when they appear.

[ALAS, WHO SHALL LIVE AFTER GOD HATH APPOINTED HIM.] The reference is to the king of Asshur who made himself into a god. The latter is noted in the Book of Isaiah. Or its meaning is: Who shall survive the decrees which God placed in the world via Asshur, for the king of Assyria conquered all the nations. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture.

OF KITTIM. They are descended from Javin, for the latter is clearly stated in Scripture (Gen. 10:4). It is also possible that Scripture alludes to the kingdom of the Greeks. I have already explained in the Book of Daniel, that the kingdom of the Greeks and that of the Kittim are one and the same. There is clear proof that it is the third beast.
FROM THE COAST OF KITTIM. Mi-yad (from the coast of) means from the place. Compare the word yad in the side (yad) of the Jordan (Num. 13:29) and Thou shalt have a place (Deut. 23:13).
AND ALSO HE. The Kittim. Kittim is singular even though it comes in the plural form. And the sons of Javan: Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim (Gen. 10:4) is proof of this.
AND BALAAM ROSE UP. For he was lying down. A deep sleep had fallen over him. Scripture clearly states, Fallen down, yet with opened eyes (v. 16).

IN SHITTIM. For Scripture clearly states, And they pitched by the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimoth even unto Abel-shittim (Num. 33:49). Everything took place in the plains of Moab, for Israel did not move from there. Also, Joshua sent spies from there (Josh. 2:1).
[AND THE PEOPLE BEGAN.] I believe that va-yachel (began) is a hifil .
AND BOWED DOWN. Israel and the daughters of Moab.

AND ISRAEL JOINED HIMSELF. The word va-yitzamed is related to the word tzemed (yoke) in a yoke of oxen (I Sam. 11:7). The reference is to the Moabite women; that is, Israel was joined with the women in the religion of pe’or .
AND HANG THEM. The reference is to those who were joined. The proof text is, And Moses said unto the judges of Israel (v. 5).

AND HANG THEM. Ve-hoka otam (and hang them) is similar to va-yaki’um (and they hanged them) in and they hanged them in the mountain (II Sam. 21:9). It is to be understood in accordance with the words of the Aramaic translation. The proof text is, In the face of the sun . The meaning of in the face of the sun is, in public. Compare, in the sight of this sun (II Sam. 12:11).
SLAY YE EVERY ONE HIS MEN. From whatever tribe they may be. It is known that they slew, even though Scripture does not mention this.
AND BROUGHT UNTO HIS BRETHREN. He gave her to his family.
WHILE THEY WERE WEEPING. Praying to God.

AND WHEN PHINEHAS…SAW. When Phinehas saw this, he rose up from the midst of the congregation, which was in the courtyard of the tent of meeting. There is a question here. It is possible to answer that Zimri (v. 14) was joined in the presence of witnesses.
INTO THE CHAMBER. El ha-kubbah (into the chamber) means into the tent. The word has a similar meaning in Arabic, although there is a difference in shape between an ohel (tent) and a kubbah (chamber).
AND THRUST. Va-yidkor (and thrust) is similar to ve-dokreni (thrust me) in and thrust me through therewith (I Sam. 31:4).

THROUGH HER BELLY. El kovatah (through her belly) means in the chamber, that is, in the chamber where she was with Zimri’s brothers. Others say that the word that kovatah is related to is the word kevah (maw) in the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw (Deut. 18:3). There is also a midrashic statement to the effect that ten miracles were performed for Phinehas. However, Scripture does not mention them.

IN THAT HE WAS VERY JEALOUS FOR MY SAKE AMONG THEM. There is no dagesh in the nun of be-kano (in that he was very jealous) in order to simplify enunciation. It means that Phinehas was jealous like his creator. Scripture tells us that God is a jealous God (Ex. 20:5) when it comes to idolatry.
[SO THAT I CONSUMED NOT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL IN MY JEALOUSY.] If Phinehas had not been jealous for My sake, then I would have destroyed all of Israel in My jealousy.

MY COVENANT OF PEACE. The meaning of beriti shalom (My covenant of peace) is: My covenant, a covenant of peace. Compare, Thy throne God (Ps. 45:7). There are many such cases. Its meaning is that Phinehas should not fear the brothers of Zimri for Zimri was a prince of a father’s house (v. 14). Phinehas was rewarded with the covenant of priesthood for himself and his seed forever, for all the high priests were descendants of Phinehas. It is possible that Eleazar had other sons.

The word acharav (after him) (v. 13) is proof that Phinehas died and is in no way to be identified with Elijah. I have already explained it. Phinehas was ruler over them [Israel] (I Chron. 9:20). He was alive during the incident of the concubine from Gibeah.
BECAUSE HE WAS JEALOUS FOR HIS GOD. He acted out of his love for God. He also did good for Israel. According to the midrashic interpretation, the father atoned and the children will atone.
WHO WAS SLAIN WITH THE MIDIANITISH WOMAN. Et ha-midyanit is to be rendered, with the Midianitish woman. There are many such instances.
A PRINCE OF A FATHER’S HOUSE AMONG THE SIMEONITES. One of the five fathers’ [houses] of the children of Simeon. The head of his father’s house was greater than he.
ZUR. Zur was one of the kings of Midian. Note, each of the five kings of Midian ruled over a house.
HARASS. Tzaror (harass) is an infinitive. It is like the word zakhor (remember) in Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy .
FOR THEY HARASS YOU. Ki tzorerim hem lakhem (for they harass you) is to be rendered: for they harassed you.
BY THEIR WILES. Be-nikhlehem (by their wiles) means by their evil thoughts. Be-nikhlehem is related to the word va-yitnakkelu (they conspired) in they conspired against him (Gen. 37:18).
AND IN THE MATTER OF COZBI. Furthermore, they intend to harm you because of what happened to Cozbi their sister.

AND IT CAME TO PASS AFTER THE PLAGUE. God spoke to Moses. He also spoke to Eleazar via Moses. And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people (Deut. 27:1) and Then sang Moses and the children of Israel (Ex. 15:1) are similar.
Scripture states after the plague because God said, Unto these the land shall be divided (v. 53).
AND MOSES AND ELEAZAR THE PRIEST SPOKE. In place of his father. It is possible that Eleazar served as Moses’ spokesman as Aaron did.
WITH THEM. Otam (with them) is similar to dabbero (speak…unto him) in speak peaceably unto him (Gen. 37:4).
FROM TWENTY YEARS OLD AND UPWARD. This means that they took the sum of the people as God commanded Moses.

[AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL, THAT CAME FORTH OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT.] Scripture states the aforementioned because there were many among those who were numbered who came out of Egypt. They most likely came to about half the number of the Israelites. Scripture starts with Reuben in imitation of the manner in which the Israelites were first numbered in the wilderness of Sinai.
WHO STROVE. The word hitzu (strove) is similar in meaning to the word yinnatzu (strive) in And if men strive together (Ex. 21:22).
WITH KORAH. I have already explained this.
AND THEY BECAME A SIGN. Compare, that they may be a sign unto the children of Israel (Num. 17:3).

NOTWITHSTANDING THE SONS OF KORAH DIED NOT. Samuel, his sons, and his grandsons who were singers and were called the Korahites is proof of this. The Book of Psalms states, For the leader; a Psalm of the sons of Korah (Ps. 49:1). The Torah also records the family of the Korahites (v. 58). Scripture mentions the sons of Korah with the sons of Reuben because the adult and the minor sons of Dathan and Abiram died. The wickedness of Dathan and Abiram was thus greater than the wickedness of Korah.

THE JAMINITES. Do not seek grammatical consistency in names. Compare, puvvah and puni (Punites) (v. 23). From shefufam Scripture derives shufami (v. 39). Scripture also reads: of yimnah (Imnah), the family of yimnah (v. 44), not ha-yemini as it does in the case of bri’ah and beri’iy (Beriites) (v. 44); Chaggi and shuni (v. 15) lacking the yod gentile. On the other hand, the yod of chaggi and shuni might be the yod gentile and the yod of the proper name is missing. The latter is correct. After Reuben, Scripture lists Simeon and Gad, who pitched next to Reuben. However, Manasseh is mentioned before Ephraim. The order is reversed in the wilderness of Sinai. It appears that this is due to their number, for the sons of Ephraim were more numerous than the sons of Manasseh in the wilderness of Sinai by eight thousand and three hundred, and in the plains of Moab the sons of Manasseh numbered more than the sons of Ephraim by twenty thousand and two hundred. No mention is made of the family of the following five sons of Benjamin: Becher, Gera, Naaman, Rosh, and Ard.

OF AHIRAM. Ahiram is the same as Ehi. Shephupham is the same as Muppim, and Hupham is the same as Huppim. The Ard and Naaman mentioned in our verse are the sons of Bela. Others say that Naaman and Ard were among those who descended to Egypt and that they are the sons of Bela the son of Benjamin.
OF SHUHAM. He is the same as Hushim.
THESE ARE THE FAMILIES OF DAN AFTER THEIR FAMILIES. For hushim was divided into many families.
THE LAND SHALL BE DIVIDED. It means that the land shall be divided among the tribes by lot.
ACCORDING TO THE LOT SHALL THEIR INHERITANCE BE DIVIDED BETWEEN THE MORE AND THE FEWER. To those who were numbered.

OF GERSHON. Scripture opens with the first-born. It mentions Gershon’s son Libni. It does not mention Shimei. It is possible that he had no children. On the other hand, Shimei might have had children and they died childless. Scripture then mentions the children of Hebron the son of Kohath. It does not name Uzziel. It then mentions the sons of Merari and goes back and refers to the sons of Itzhar. Then it mentions the sons of Amram. Scripture places them last because it goes on to explain what happened to the grandsons of Amram.

THE KORAHITES. They are the sons of Korah. Scripture mentions Jochebed out of respect to her sons. It does not speak of her mother, because Scripture is being brief. Asriel, whom she bore (I Chron. 7:14) is similar.

AND THEY THAT WERE NUMBERED. The Levites. The Levites increased by seven hundred in this numbering. It is amazing that the Levites increased by only seven hundred. Look! The Israelites from among whom all those above the age of twenty died numbered about the same as they did during their first numbering. [The small increase in the number of Levites is strange] for the Levites were not included in the numbering of Israel. Eleazar the Kohen proves the latter.
BUT AMONG THESE THERE WAS NOT A MAN. This verse refers to the number of the children of Israel.
SAVE CALEB THE SON OF JEPHUNNEH. Caleb is mentioned before Joshua, following God’s word.
AND HE WAS NOT AMONG THE COMPANY. The daughters thought that the children of those who gathered themselves together against the Lord would not inherit.

BUT HE DIED IN HIS OWN SIN. Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi the Spaniard says but he died in his own sin is to be understood as connected to and he had no sons . It is as we say today, such and such occurred to so and so because of his sins. This interpretation is not far off.
BECAUSE HE HAD NO SON. Ki en lo ben is to be rendered, because he had no son.
RIGHT. Ken means true. Or, the thing is so.
AND THOU SHALT CAUSE THE INHERITANCE. What he should have received, they shall receive.
AND HAVE NO SON. This is proof that a son inherits his father’s property.
UNTO HIS BRETHREN. From his father or mother.
UNTO HIS KINSMAN THAT IS NEXT TO HIM. From all of his family.

AND HE SHALL POSSESS IT. The inheritance. I have already explained the approach of the rabbis in my comments on unto a foreign people (Ex. 21:8). We need rabbinic tradition to know the laws of inheritance with regard to whether a father or a mother inherits a son’s property or what a woman inherits.

The rabbis of blessed memory said that the chapter that opens with the words, Get thee up into this mountain (v. 12), follows the laws of inheritance because Moses wanted to know who would inherit his position.

TO SANCTIFY ME. The word le-hakdesheni (to sanctify me) is connected to meritem (ye rebelled). Its meaning is, ye rebelled with regard to sanctifying me. This, I have explained, is the meaning of because ye sanctified Me not in the midst of the children of Israel (Deut. 32:51).
THE GOD OF THE SPIRITS. He knows the spirits. He knows which spirit is fit.
[SET.] The word yifkod (set) is related to the word pakid (official).
WHO MAY GO OUT BEFORE THEM. In war.
WHO MAY LEAD THEM OUT. Va-asher yotzi’em (who may lead them out) means who will direct someone else to lead them out.
IN WHOM IS SPIRIT. Now all living persons have spirit in them. Its meaning can only be similar to that of be thou strong therefore, and show thyself a man (I Kings 2:2).
AND LAY THY HAND UPON HIM. To show Israel that he was in Moses’ place and that he was the one on whom Moses had placed his hands.
AND THOU SHALT PUT OF THY HONOR UPON HIM. You will honor Joshua in front of all of Israel.
THAT…MAY HEARKEN. For Israel already believes in you. When they see that you honored Joshua they will respect him, for they will follow your ways.
AT HIS WORD SHALL THEY GO OUT. Upon the word of Eleazar by the judgment of the Urim. Others say, in accordance to the judgment of the Urim. The first interpretation appears correct to me.
BOTH HE, AND ALL THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. In regard to that which pertains to all.
EVEN ALL THE CONGREGATION. They gathered in the tent of meeting concerning a matter that pertained to the congregation.

The reason the chapter dealing with the sacrifices follows is that God then ordered Moses to command the children of Israel regarding the sacrifices they are obligated to offer, for Moses was not to enter the land with them. Scripture starts with the daily burnt offering even though it was mentioned earlier. It is possible that the earlier burnt offering was the one offered at Mount Sinai. On the other hand, it is possible that Scripture wants to insure that the arrangement of the sacrifices is in order.
MY FOOD. I have previously explained the meaning of the term lechem (food).

MADE BY FIRE. I have previously explained the meaning of le-ishai (made by fire). The meaning of lachmi le-ishai re’ach nicho’ach (My food…made by fire, of a sweet savour unto Me) is, food for my fire, for a sweet savour unto Me.
IN ITS DUE SEASON. It shall not be bought before the morning, nor delayed after evening.

THE ONE LAMB. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen the Spaniard says that our verse is abridged. It should be read as if written ha-keves, keves echad (the lamb, one lamb). However, I believe that the heh of keves is to be read as if written twice. I have already shown you many such cases.

WHICH WAS OFFERED IN MOUNT SINAI. Its meaning is, as you offered on Mount Sinai. This verse is an additional proof that Israel did not offer burnt offerings in the wilderness after they journeyed from Sinai, as I previously explained with perfect proof.
SHALT THOU POUR OUT A DRINK-OFFERING OF STRONG DRINK. The stem nun is swallowed by the samekh . We will rely on the words of our sages of blessed memory as to its meaning.

OF EVERY SABBATH. The vav suffixed to the word shabbat refers to the day of Sabbath. This is so even though we find the word me-challelo (from profaning it) in Every one that keepeth the sabbath from profaning it (Is. 56:6). The meaning of be-shabbato (of every Sabbath) is, every sabbath and sabbath . Compare, yom be-yomo (daily) (Ex. 5:13).
BESIDE THE CONTINUAL BURNT-OFFERING. This means after the continual burnt offering. The Sabbath burnt offering shall follow it.

AND IN YOUR NEW MOONS. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen the Spaniard, who rests in paradise, says that u-ve-roshe chodshekhem (and in your new moons) refers to the new moon of Nisan, for Scripture clearly states, it shall be the first month of the year to you (Ex. 12:2). Scripture then goes on to say, This is the burnt-offering of every new moon (v. 14), that is, they shall offer this burnt offering on every new moon. The Torah therefore adds, throughout the months of the year ( Ibid. ). Rabbi Moses’ interpretation is correct. He is right even though the yod in u-ve-roshe chodshekhem (and in your new moons) argues against his interpretation. However, the fact that we find hinneh chodesh machar (Behold, tomorrow is the new moon) (I Sam. 20:5) shows that what he says is correct.

OF EVERY NEW MOON. Chodesh be-chodsho (of every new moon) is similar to shabbat be-shabbato (of every sabbath) (Num. 28 :10). According to the plain meaning of the text there is no possibility of interpreting it any other way, for there is no mention of the moon in our verse. Furthermore, we only find the Hebrew form for the verb new in the pi’el , which has a dagesh placed in it. However, here the dalet has no dagesh in it.

AND ONE HE-GOAT FOR A SIN-OFFERING UNTO THE LORD. Compare, upon which the lot fell for the Lord, and offer him for a sin-offering (Lev. 16:9). Note, in Hebrew the sin is connected to the sinner whenever the word chattat is followed by a lamed . Can’t you see that Scripture reads, ve-chatati le-avi (I shall bear the blame to my father) (Gen. 44:32). Look, this is contrary to the midrashic interpretation. However, the midrashic interpretation has a secret meaning.
ON THE FOURTEENTH DAY OF THE MONTH. Scripture does not mention at dusk. This verse is also a support for those who transmit tradition, even though their words need no support.

AND ONE HE-GOAT FOR A SIN-OFFERING. U-se’ir chattat echad (and he-goat for a sin-offering) is the same as u-se’ir izzim echad le-chattat (and one he-goat for a sin-offering). Our verse is abridged. Observe, Scripture does not mention the Sabbath burnt offering which is to be brought during the seven days of Passover. It similarly omits the burnt offering which accompanied the waved sheaf. We need tradition. For the verse (v. 10) tells us that [the burnt offering] of every sabbath shall follow the daily burnt offering.

WHEN YE BRING A NEW MEAL-OFFERING UNTO THE LORD. The two waveloaves were the main offerings. The seven lambs, one young bullock, two rams and two lambs of peace offering were brought along with it. The burnt offering mentioned in our chapter refers to the obligatory sacrifice of the festival day. The fact that Scripture does not state anything at all about the Sabbath and festivals, but only mentions And ye shall bring an offering made by fire without telling us the number of sacrificial animals for the festival of unleavened bread (Lev. 23:8), and Sukkot (Lev. 23:36), and the holiday celebrated on the tenth day of Tishri (Lev. 23:27) is proof of the words of our sages. The same is true for the day of the shofar sounding. Scripture does not mention the new moon burnt offering. And the continual burnt-offering and the meal-offering thereof (Num. 29:6) refers to the first burnt offering.

IT IS A DAY OF BLOWING THE HORN. It is a commandment to sound a tru’ah . If this statement referred to the burnt offering offered on this day, then why is it not mentioned with regard to the other festivals? Furthermore, the Torah tells us to sound a teki’ah over the burnt offerings, not a tru’ah .

ONE YOUNG BULLOCK. Brought by the congregation. The same applies to one ram. The reference is not to the bullock and ram offered by the kohen gadol (high priest).I believe that the ram mentioned in the Torah portion Achare mot, which the kohen took from the people, is not the ram mentioned in our verse, for Scripture says, with regard to the high priest’s ram and the ram of the people, and offer his burnt-offering and the burnt-offering of the people (Lev. 16:24). The fact that there are seven additional lambs is proof of this. The one he-goat for a sin offering is not to be identified with one of the he-goats chosen by lot. Scripture therefore states, beside the sin-offering of atonement (v. 11) mentioned in the Torah portion Achare mot .
A SOLEMN ASSEMBLY. I have already explained the meaning of the term atzeret (a solemn assembly).
OR YOUR MEAL-OFFERINGS, OR YOUR DRINK-OFFERINGS. To each and every burnt offering, in accordance with its law.

UNTO THE HEADS OF THE TRIBES. I believe that this section followed the war with Midian. The Midianite war therefore comes after it. Compare, And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses (Num. 12:1), which comes after and they abode in Hazeroth (Num. 11:35) as I explained. Scripture tells us that the children of Gad came to Moses and Eleazar and the princes of the congregation, and spoke their piece (Num. 32:2-6). Scripture then writes, So Moses gave charge concerning them to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of the fathers’ houses (Num. 32:28). The heads of the fathers’ houses refers to the already-mentioned princes (Num. 32:2). Moses told the children of Gad and the children of Reuben, and do that which hath proceeded out of your mouth (Num. 32:24). Scripture therefore reads, And Moses spoke unto the heads of the tribes . saying… (v. 2). When a man voweth a vow…he shall not break his word . Scripture there writes, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth (v. 3).
OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. That they should relate this to the children of Israel.
UNTO THE LORD. He mentions God’s name. He vows as follows: If this comes to pass, then I will give the following sum to God, or I will fast.
SWEARETH. Hishavah (sweareth) is an infinitive. It is connected to a noun. There are many such cases.

HE SHALL NOT BREAK HIS WORD. Lo yahel (he shall not break) means he shall not profane. The word yahel is not related to the word mechilah (forgiveness). We need tradition, for Scripture speaks of a man and a women but does not tell us at what age a person is considered a man or at what age a female is considered a women.
AND BINDETH HERSELF BY A BOND. Or bindeth herself by a bond.[5.] HER BOND. Essarah (her bond) belongs to a different form. It is not the same as issar (bond).
DISALLOW. The word heni (disallow) means broke or nullified. Compare, tenu’ati (My displeasure) (Num. 14:34).
IN THE DAY THAT HE HEARETH. And not on any other day.
WHILE HER VOWS ARE UPON HER. In her father’s house. If her father does not nullify her vows, her husband may disallow her vows.
HE HEARETH IT. The word from her mouth.
AND THE CLEAR UTTERANCE OF HER LIPS. The oath.

AND IF A WOMAN VOWED IN HER HUSBAND’S HOUSE. If the widow vowed in an earlier time and her husband disallowed it, then she does not have to keep the vow in her widowhood. This speaks about a vow which she vowed regarding the future, and the husband died before the vow was to take effect. The meaning of selichah (forgiveness) has been previously explained.
TO AFFLICT THE SOUL. Even to afflict the soul. I have already explained that “affliction of the soul” refers to fasting.

THEN HE CAUSETH ALL HER VOWS TO STAND. He has already caused all of her vows to stand. Scripture then explains how he caused her vows to stand, namely, because he held his peace in the day that he heard them.
THEN HE SHALL BEAR HER INIQUITY. For she is under his care.
BETWEEN A MAN AND HIS WIFE. His wife being a woman who is an adult.
BETWEEN A FATHER AND HIS DAUGHTER. If she has not reached adulthood. Hence Scripture reads, being in her youth .
ARM YE MEN. The meaning of hechaletzu (arm ye men) is, gird your men of war.
TO EXECUTE THE LORD’S VENGEANCE. The reference is to Israel’s vengeance because they were enticed into worshipping idols.
SO WERE DELIVERED. Va-yimasseru means and they were delivered. The word li-mesor (to deliver) (v. 16) is close in meaning to it.
WITH THE HOLY VESSELS. The ark.
AND THEY SLEW EVERY MALE. Adult males.
AND ZUR. The father of Cozbi.

BALAAM ALSO THE SON OF BEOR. Some say that after Balaam returned to his place, he went back to Midian as soon as he learned of the plague that struck Israel because of his advice. He came back to receive money from the elders of Midian.
AND ALL THEIR GOODS. The word chelam (their goods) is a general term. It refers to gold, silver, copper, iron, and garments.
AND ALL THEIR CITIES IN THE PLACES WHEREIN THEY DWELT. An all-inclusive term followed by a limiting term.
AND ALL THEIR ENCAMPMENTS. Tirotam (their encampments) means the palaces of the kings.
AND THEY TOOK ALL THE SPOIL, AND ALL THE PREY. Malko’ach (prey) is a general term for men and cattle.
THE CAPTIVES. Shevi (captive) is a specific term. It refers to humans.
THE SPOIL. Shalal (spoil) refers to garments.

WITH THE OFFICERS OF THE HOST. The word pekudai (officers of) is related to the word yifkod (set) in Let the Lord…set (Num. 27 :16). It is similar to pekide he-chayil . Similarly, the word keru’e (the elect of) (Num. 1:16) means the same as keri’e (the elect of) (Num. 16:2).
THE CAPTAINS OF THOUSANDS AND THE CAPTAINS OF HUNDREDS. They totaled one hundred and thirty-two.

HAVE YE SAVED ALL THE WOMEN ALIVE. The meaning of kol nekevah (all the women) is, even one woman. En kol (had nothing) (II Sam. 12:3) is similar. It is also possible that have ye saved all the women alive is to be taken literally, for they kept all the females alive. There are many such instances.
THE LITTLE ONES. Taf (little ones) is a general term for male and female minors.
YE AND YOUR CAPTIVES. Because of the glory which dwells among you.

AND ALL WORK OF GOATS’ HAIR. This is to be interpreted in accordance with my earlier explanation. Observe, the garment is unclean because it touched a corpse. The meaning of our verse is, the garments shall be with you until you are purified. On the other hand, titchate’u (ye shall purify) might be transitive. Ve-hitavvitem lakhem (and ye shall mark out) (Num. 34:10) is similar, for gevul (line) is the object.
AND ELEAZAR THE PRIEST SAID. For the law regarding the cow was given to Eleazar. Moses told the people in a general manner, ye shall purify (v. 20). However, Eleazar explained it to them.
THE TIN. The meaning of the bedil (tin) is known.

NEVERTHELESS IT SHALL BE PURIFIED WITH THE WATER OF SPRINKLING. It would have appeared to us that the reference is to the mixture of the water and tahe ashes of the cow, as in because the water of sprinkling was not dashed against him (Num. 19:13). However, our wise men of blessed memory say that its meaning is, in the amount of water in which a menstruant bathes. Their mind is much greater than our minds.
TAKE THE SUM. I have already explained the meaning of sa et rosh (take the sum).
OF THE PREY. Malko’ach (the prey) refers to the cattle.
THAT WAS TAKEN. Ha-shevi (that was taken) refers to humans. A vav is missing, as in shemesh yare’ach (sun moon) (Hab. 3:11).
AND THE HEADS OF THE FATHERS’ HOUSES OF THE CONGREGATION. The reference is to the princes.
AND DIVIDE THE PREY. Malko’ach (prey) is a general term.
ONE SOUL. Echad nefesh means the same as nefesh echad (one soul).
ONE DRAWN. Achuz (drawn) is similar to ve-ha’achuz achuz (and proportionally) (I Chron. 24:6). As I have explained, they are connected.
EVEN OF ALL THE CATTLE. Camels. Look, Eleazar did not take a portion from them. Perhaps they were few. Hence neither the number which they brought nor the amount which the Levites took is mentioned.

OVER AND ABOVE THE BOOTY. Aside from what they consumed. Scripture therefore reads yeter (above). The Torah mentions the amount of spoil because it consisted of a vast number. We never heard of a similar amount of spoil. Scripture also mentions the tribute, for it too was very great. The word mekhes (tribute) (v. 37) comes from a double root. It is vocalized like the word memer (bitterness) in and bitterness to her that bore him (Prov. 17:25). Mekhes is related to the word takhossu (ye shall make your count) in ye shall make your count for the lamb (Ex. 12:4). The meaning of mekhes (tribute) is a portion.
[BOTH OF MAN AND OF BEAST.] Scripture states both of man and of beast . Man and beast are general terms.
THE OFFICERS. I have already explained this term.
THAT ARE UNDER OUR CHARGE. Asher be-yadenu means that they were in their charge. Compare, yadekh (in your hands) in And take with thee ten loaves in your hands (I Kings 14:3).
AND WE HAVE BROUGHT. In thought or by mouth.
ARMLETS. Etzadah (armlet) is an ornament placed on the arm. This is explicitly stated in Scripture.
AND BRACELETS. A tzamid (bracelet) is an ornament placed on the wrist.
SIGNET-RINGS. Taba’at (signet ring) refers to an ornament placed on the finger.
EAR-RINGS. Agil is an earring. This is clearly stated in Scripture. This ornament is possibly so called because it is round ( agul ).
GIRDLES. Kumaz (girdles) is similar to its neighboring objects.
EVEN ALL THE WROUGHT JEWELS. Scripture tells us that there was no broken object among them.
FOR THE MEN OF WAR HAD TAKEN BOOTY, EVERY MAN FOR HIMSELF. Scripture mentions this to inform us that each one of the men of war took a vast amount of gold and wrought articles.
THE CHILDREN OF REUBEN. For he was the son of the mistress.
WAS A PLACE FOR CATTLE. For there it was good pasture.
THE CHILDREN OF GAD…CAME. They thought of this first. Hence Scripture places them first.

AND THEY SAID…LET THIS LAND BE GIVEN. Scripture repeats, and they said because they spoke at length. Some say that the word et is the object of yuttan (be given). I do not know why. Look, Scripture reads: netam eretz (the land is burnt up) (Is. 9:18); yechalek ha-aretz (the land shall be divided) (Num. 26:55); ve-lo nasa otom ha-aretz (and the land was not able to bear them) (Gen. 13:6); and asher hu va shammah be-kirbo (whither they go to be among them) (Deut. 31:16).
YE TURN AWAY. Teniyun (ye turn away) means you break.
FOR WHEN THEY WENT UP UNTO THE VALLEY OF ESHCOL. For those who went up to the north, went to the south.

THEY HAVE NOT WHOLLY FOLLOWED ME. There is no dagesh in the lamed of mile’u (wholly followed). Mile’u is a pi’el . Compare, malle (fill) in fill thy horn with oil (I Sam. 16:1). They did not complete what they started.

CALEB THE SON OF JEPHUNNEH. Caleb is mentioned first, as in the case of God’s oath. The word mile’u (wholly followed) is similar to the word bikshu (have sought) in have sought after my soul (Ps. 44:5) and shilchu (they have set) in They have set Thy sanctuary on fire (Ps. 74:7).
AND HE MADE THEM WANDER. Va-yeni’em (and he made them wander) is related to the word na (a fugitive) in a fugitive and a wanderer (Gen. 4:12). Scripture reads va-yeni’em because they did not rest.

A BROOD. The word tarbut (a brood) is connected to the word ribbiti (brought up) in That I have dandled and brought up (Lam. 2:22). It is close in meaning to the word rav (officers) in all the officers (rav) of his house (Esther 1:8). The meaning of tarbut is, grown up in years.

TO AUGMENT. Li-sepot (to augment) means the same as le-hosif (to add). However, it comes from a different root. The word sofu (add) in Add…unto your sacrifices (Jer. 7:21) is similar, for we do not find this root among the stems that begin with a yod and drop the yod in the kal .
AND CITIES. First for our little ones.

READY. The word chushim (ready) is vocalized like the word mulim (circumcised) in were circumcised (Josh. 5:5). It means quickly. It is related to the word chushah (hasten) in Make speed, hasten, stay not (I Sam. 20:38).
AND FORWARD. The word ve-hale’ah (and forward) is used with regard to both place and time. The meaning of ve-hale’ah is, and above.
UNTIL HE HATH DRIVEN OUT. God.
BEFORE THE LORD. For the ark was there. Before the Lord is to be taken as I have explained, for the phrase is always used in a positive sense.
FOR YOUR SHEEP. The alef in tzonakhem (your sheep) is superfluous. It is like the alef in he’eznichu (become foul) in and the rivers shall become foul (Is. 19:6).

EVERY MAN THAT IS ARMED FOR WAR. Kol chalutz tzava (every man that is armed for war) is similar to ha-aron ha-berit (the ark of the covenant) (Josh. 3:14). Its meaning is, every man armed, armed for war .
THEN YE SHALL GIVE THEM. The meaning of u-netattem la-hem is, you shall give them. The vav is like the Arabic fa , for such is the rule of the language.

THEY SHALL HAVE POSSESSIONS AMONG YOU. He gave them respect, for the meaning of our verse is, if they will not go armed before you, then you shall force them to go with you and they shall have possessions among you. Or, if they change their minds, then they shall have possessions among you. The word ve-nochazu (they shall have possessions) follows the rules of a root that has a yod as its first letter, for the letters alef, heh, vav , and yod interchange.
AND THE CHILDREN OF GAD…ANSWERED. A second time for emphasis.
WE WILL PASS. The form nachnu (we) is the original form of the word. The alef in anachnu (we) is added. The half tribe of Manasseh is not mentioned until now because it was but half a tribe.
AND NEBO. It is likely that the reference is to Mount Nebo, where, as I shall explain, Moses was buried.
THEIR NAMES BEING CHANGED. These cities had their names changed. The same applies to Sibmah.
AND DISPOSSESSED. Some say that Machir was alive. However, I believe that and dispossessed refers to the warrior that was in the family.
[UNTO MACHIR THE SON OF MANASSEH.] The meaning of unto Machir the son of Manasseh is, unto the sons of Machir the son of Manasseh. Compare, And Judah said unto Simeon his brother (Jud. 1:3).

AND JAIR THE SON OF MANASSEH. Jair was from the family of Judah. This is explicitly stated. For Hezron took the daughter of Machir the son of Manasseh, and she bore him Segub. Segub begot Jair, who had cities among the cities of Gilead. Jair is called after his mother’s family. There were also kohanim who were called after the name of the children of Barzillai the Gileadite. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture. This is no reason to ask: How did Jair inherit among another tribe, for it was the land of Canaan that was divided, not the land of the Amorites that was on the eastern side of the Jordan, for there were Amorites in the land of Canaan and they were the mightiest of the seven nations.
THE VILLAGES THEREOF. Chavvotehem (villages thereof) is to be interpreted in context. It means walled cities.

THESE ARE THE STAGES. Moses recorded all the journeys of the Israelites when the children of Israel camped in the plains of Moab and stayed there for a number of months, until the afore-mentioned cities were built. They did not move from there until Aaron died.
THEIR GOINGS FORTH. How they went from place to place. Therefore their goings forth follows.
BY THE COMMANDMENT OF THE LORD. This is connected to stage by stage .
ON THE MORROW AFTER THE PASSOVER. I have explained this, and with a high hand (Ex. 14:8) as well.
UPON THEIR GODS ALSO THE LORD EXECUTED JUDGMENTS. As in the incident with Dagan’s head. For God said so to Moses.
AND TURNED BACK. This alludes to the cloud or to Israel.
FROM PENE-HAHIROTH. Pene-hahirot and Pi-hahiroth refers to the same place. The mouth is in the face.
THREE DAYS’ JOURNEY. I have already explained this.
KIBROTH-HATTAAVAH. The latter is in Kadesh-barnea, as I explained.
AND THEY JOURNEYED FROM KADESH. Kadesh is the name of a city.
[AND THE CANAANITE…HEARD.] Scripture tells us this here because the Canaanite fought with Israel at Hor ha-Hor.
ZALMONAH, AND…PUNON. I have explained this.
ALMON-DIBLATHAIM. This is a general term for many journeys, as I explained in the Torah portion, This is the statute of the law (Num. 19:2).
FROM BETH-JESHIMOTH. This is the valley which looks down upon the wasteland. God then commanded Moses to warn Israel because they were soon to pass over.
THEIR FIGURED STONES. Maskiyyotam (their figured stones) is similar to ve-even maskit (any figured stone) (Lev. 26:1).
THEIR HIGH PLACES. Bamotam means their high places. Compare, bamate aretz (the high places of the earth) (Is. 58:14).
AND YE SHALL INHERIT THE LAND. Ve-hitnachaltem (and ye shall inherit) is similar to ve-hitavvitem (and ye shall mark out) (Num. 34 :10). Ha-aretz (the land) is the object.
Scripture mentions to the more ye shall give the more inheritance to connect But if ye will not drive out the inhabitants (v. 55) which comes after it.

AS THORNS. Sikkim refers to sharp thorns. It is related to the word mesukkato (hedge thereof) in the hedge thereof (Is. 5:5) and the word sakh (hedge) in behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns (Hos. 2:8).

AND AS PRICKS. The word tzeninim (pricks) is to be explained according to its context. It means the same as u-leshotet be-tziddekhem (a scourge in your sides) (Josh. 23:13), which refers to a blow delivered by a whip. On the other hand, the word tzeninim (pricks) might refer to sharp thorns, as in Thorns (tzinnim) and snares in the way of the froward (Prov. 22:5). Observe, Scripture further explains the borders of their inheritance from which they are obligated to expel the inhabitants of the land.

INTO THE LAND OF CANAAN. Ha-aretz kena’an (the land of Canaan) is similar to ve-hanevu’ah oded ha-navi (even the prophecy of Oded the prophet) (II Chron. 15:8), the meaning of which is, the prophecy, prophecy of Oded the prophet. The meaning of our clause is, the land, land of Canaan.
BY THE SIDE OF EDOM. The word yede (side of) means place of. Compare, by the side of (yad) the Jordan (Num. 13:29).
UNTO THE BROOK OF EGYPT. Nachlah mitzrayim means unto the brook of Egypt. It does not refer to the Nile.
THE GREAT SEA. The Spanish sea. The meaning of our verse is: And the Great Sea shall be your western border. The Great Sea itself shall serve as the border.
AND YE SHALL MARK OUT. The alef in ve-hitavvitem (and ye shall mark out) is in place of a vav . Compare, ve-hitvita tav (and set a mark) (Ezek. 9:4). This is so, even though the forms differ.
AND YE SHALL MARK OUT. Ve-hitavvitem (and ye shall mark out) is similar to the word ta’avat (utmost bound) in Unto the utmost bound of the everlasting hills (Gen. 49:26).
AND SHALL STRIKE. The word machah (strike) is to be interpreted as the ancients did. It means it shall break. It is related to the word yimcha’u (clap) in Let the floods clap their hands (Ps. 98:8).
THE TWO TRIBES. Scripture mentions this a second time in order to explain the place of their inheritance.
SHALL TAKE POSSESSION. Yinchalu (shall take possession) is a causative. The same applies to the word u-nechaltanu (and take us for Thine inheritance) (Ex. 34:9) in the opinion of the grammarians.

ELEAZAR. He is mentioned first because Joshua went out by his command. Furthermore, Eleazar was also the son of Aaron. Scripture does not mention the princes of the tribes of Reuben or Gad, for they had already taken their share. The commentaries say that Scripture starts with Judah, for that is the way the lot came out at first. However, there is a great argument against them. Nevertheless, the comments appear correct to us.
PEDAHEL. If the heh in Pedahel is silent then we have two words each with its own meaning, for the heh is not an implied letter.
AND OPEN LAND. The meaning of migrash (open land) is known.
INTO THE LAND OF CANAAN. The meaning of artzah kena’an (into the land of Canaan) is known. This chapter, like others, is connected.
THEN YE SHALL APPOINT YOU CITIES. The word ve-hikritem (then shall ye appoint you) is related to the word kiryah (cities).

FOR THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. This is not connected to the previous verse, for the preceding verse states that these cities will be cities of refuge. However, it does not state for whom they shall serve as cities of refuge. Scripture then explains that these six cities shall serve as cities of refuge for the children of Israel, and for the stranger…who lives among them .
WHEN HE MEETETH HIM. The feh of bi-figo (when he meeteth him) is vocalized with a chirik like the word shivri (I break) in when I break (Lev. 26:26), for vocalization changes in the infinitive.
AND IF HE THRUST HIM. From a high place.
OR HURLED AT HIM. An inclining wall or a deadly object.
LYING IN WAIT. I have previously explained the meaning of bi-tzediyyah (lying in wait).
SUDDENLY. The meaning of be-feta is suddenly.
SEEING HIM NOT. Re’ot is an infinitive.
AND HE WAS NOT HIS ENEMY. He had no intention of seeking his harm.

THEREIN UNTIL THE DEATH OF THE HIGH PRIEST. Some say that the meaning of until the death of is, until the investigation of. They compare it to And wisdom shall die with you (Job. 12:2). However, what they say is worthless. For And wisdom shall die with you means exactly what it says, as does until the death of the high priest . For the high priest atones on behalf of Israel, and this incident happened during his lifetime.
THE BORDER OF HIS CITY. Et gevul means beyond the border. Compare, et ha-ir (out of the city) in as I am gone out of the city (Ex. 9:29).
BLOODGUILTINESS. I have already explained the meaning of dam (bloodguiltiness).
SO YE SHALL NOT POLLUTE. Do evil in secret.
SHED IT. Shofkho (shed it) is a verb. Compare go’alo (his redeemer) in then shall his redeemer…come (Lev. 25:25).

AND THOU SHALT NOT DEFILE THE LAND. The pollution shall not defile the land. Or it is a command. The land shall not be polluted because I dwell among them. I do not dwell there out of respect for the land but out of respect for the children of Israel. Therefore Scripture says, I the Lord dwell in the midst of the children of Israel (v. 34).

CAME NEAR. This chapter also is connected to the one that comes before it. When Moses commanded the Israelites to give the Levites cities from the inheritance of Israel [the heads of the fathers’ houses drew near].
THE HEADS OF THE FATHERS’ HOUSES. The reference is to the princes.
AND WHEN THE JUBILEE…SHALL BE. Even if the jubilee shall be, we have no hope of the inheritance returning to us, for it shall be added to the inheritance of the tribe.
THE TRIBE OF THE SONS OF JOSEPH SPEAKETH RIGHT. For the heads of the fathers’ houses spoke on behalf of the entire tribe.
[SO SHALL NO INHERITANCE OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL REMOVE FROM TRIBE TO TRIBE.] The meaning of tissov (remove) is, shall not turn from here to there, be it from them or from others.
The meaning of so shall no inheritance be removed is, no inheritance shall be removed from this day and onward even though they had not as yet inherited the land.

AND EVERY DAUGHTER, THAT POSSESSETH AN INHERITANCE. After the inheritance of the land. Scripture therefore states a second time, So shall no inheritance remove [ from one tribe to another tribe ] (v. 9).
MAHLAH, TIRZAH. Scripture first mentioned them in the order of their birth. It now mentions them in the order in which they were first taken by men in marriage.
THEY WERE MARRIED INTO THE FAMILIES. This is a sign that their cousins were not all brothers.
THESE ARE THE COMMANDMENTS. Relating to inheritance, vows, and every daughter that possesseth an inheritance, and the laws regarding bloodshed.
BY THE JORDAN AT JERICHO. On the eastern bank.
